design_rationale:
WORKLOG — crop_input_desk task 0 (Merrill Hollenbeck, Hollenbeck Ridge Farms)

STEP 0. DIFFICULTY PRE-CHECK, ASSET LEDGER AND SCOPE CLAIM
Read first: references/product_extended.yaml, references/task_tools.py, references/task.json; then
blueprint/blueprint.yaml, blueprint/products/agronomy.yaml, blueprint/db_schema.json and
blueprint/share_tools.py. Base closes: eleven base policies, six programmes with a complete
parameter_schema, four measures, thirteen event types, and a share-tool layer that can locate and
read every table this difficulty needs. Identity threshold K = 2 (VERIFICATION_MATCH_THRESHOLD in
share_tools.py), credential params member_number / phone_number / email / tax_id_last4 /
membership_since.

Draw, run before any of the tree or the computations was designed:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py \
      env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/tasks/crop_input_desk --tasks 2
  {"task": 0, "key": "farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/crop_input_desk/0",
   "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/crop_input_desk/1",
   "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}
Task 0 therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems (three problems in all) and its three
computations carry 6, 6 and 4 declared factors. Assignment chosen: the settlement payment 6, the
service charge 6, the return credit 4.

Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is first). Claimed by this task: the base subjects
agronomy_credit_memo_issued, agronomy_finance_charge_assessed and agronomy_payment_posted, with
the base policies agronomy_returns_and_credits, agronomy_finance_charge and
agronomy_payment_application as their lineage, and the three task tools issue_return_credit_6859ca91,
assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa and post_member_arrears_payment_ad47b93a. Left free for
task 1, whose draw calls for one prerequisite problem and two computations of four factors each:
agronomy_discount_granted (the season volume discount) and agronomy_prepay_booked (the prepay
booking ceiling), with agronomy_discount_schedule and agronomy_prepay_program as their lineage and
two further tools. Those two problems form their own chain — the closed season's discount must
stand on the ledger before the ceiling that is measured on that season's net spend can be worked
out — so task 1 has an independent, load-bearing space of its own and neither task rewrites the
other's dependency. Deliberately left unclaimed by both tasks: agronomy_account_updated (whose
account_live_for_maintenance gate has mixed authority over a single-field correlation group and so
cannot be satisfied), agronomy_invoice_issued, agronomy_account_suspended and the lifecycle
subjects.

Design thesis. Surface goal: "what do I have to send you today to get buying again". Scored core
parameter: the settlement figure the member remits. Between the two lie two policy prerequisites
the customer never mentions — the credit owed for product already back at the plant, and the
service charge owed for the statement month then running — because the settlement figure is a
share of a balance that both of them move. Draft chain: surface goal -> the settlement figure is a
share of the account's overdue balance plus a share of the service charges standing -> the service
charge for the month is not yet on the ledger -> the service charge is worked on an overdue balance
that must already carry every credit owed -> the credit for the returned chemical is not yet on the
ledger. Depth 2 prerequisite hops; breadth at each hop from history windows (ten and twelve
statement months, the six-month terms split, the three-month recent window), from tier parameters
of the Seasonal Terms programme, and from three other product lines (custom, storage, grain and
patronage). Terminal state: three new rows on agronomy_invoices — a credit memo, a service charge
and the member's own payment — in that order.

Per-computation factor draft (baseline and intended tier, before the world was laid out):
  return credit (4): restocking rate; the price the credit is computed at; the handling figure
    withheld; the share of the restocking charge waived for field-services members.
  service charge (6): the monthly rate; the anchor the overdue clock runs from; the days of grace;
    the relief for stored grain; the share of granted discounts added back; the collection sum.
  settlement payment (6): the reinstatement share; the grain credit; the rounding of the quoted
    figure; the share of standing service charges carried in; the patronage cash offset; the age
    step.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
  root: agronomy_ext_arrears_settlement_payment (what the caller asks for)
  edge 1: agronomy_ext_arrears_settlement_payment <- agronomy_ext_arrears_service_charge
    kind value_input; gate charges_standing (a compute binding of the blocked policy); form state;
    prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the blocked policy's own rule: "The figure that
    settles the arrears on a crop input account is fixed only once that account's ledger carries the
    service charge due on its overdue invoices for the statement month then running."
    handling-time condition: the ledger carries that charge. resolved by
    assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa, owner agent.
    false at the opening: initial_state.agronomy_invoices.<FC1>.posted_date = 2026-04-30 is the only
    service charge on the ledger, while initial_state.agronomy_invoices.<I0>.due_date = 2026-03-07
    and initial_state.agronomy_accounts.<ACCT_A>.past_due_since = 2026-03-08 show a further month
    has run. deletion sensitivity: skip it and payment_amount moves 37030.00 -> 36940.00.
  edge 2: agronomy_ext_arrears_service_charge <- agronomy_ext_crop_protection_return_credit
    kind value_input; gate overdue_balance; form state; prerequisite sentence: "The service charge
    on a crop input account is worked out only once every credit memo owed for crop protection
    product that has come back to the plant stands written against that account."
    handling-time condition: every credit memo owed for returned product stands written. resolved by
    issue_return_credit_6859ca91, owner agent.
    false at the opening: initial_state.agronomy_orders.<OR_RET>.order_status = approved and
    .signed_by_member = True record the product already back at the plant, while the only credit memo
    on the ledger is initial_state.agronomy_invoices.<CM1>.posted_date = 2025-10-27 against a
    different delivery. deletion sensitivity: skip it and service_charge_amount moves
    320.20 -> 361.10, which carries into payment_amount as well.
  topological order: return credit -> service charge -> settlement payment.
  parallel edges: none. The tree is a chain, so no two writes could be reordered at all.
  four-point test, edge 1: (1) ordering connective "only once"; (2) the side waited on is a
  record-visible state — a service-charge entry standing on the account's ledger — with no action,
  performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token, no row id;
  (4) strength "only once ... carries", which is exactly the edge's condition, neither wider (it
  does not demand every charge ever due) nor narrower (it does not name a particular invoice).
  four-point test, edge 2: (1) "only once"; (2) a record-visible state — a credit memo standing
  written against the account; (3) no code names; (4) it covers exactly the credits owed for
  returned product and nothing else.
  state form available on both edges, so no fallback is declared. Exactly one write of this
  difficulty brings each state about: only assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa writes a service
  charge row on a crop input account, and only issue_return_credit_6859ca91 writes a credit memo.
  Derivation a reader performs for edge 2: the sentence says the charge waits on every credit memo
  owed for returned product standing on the account; find_agronomy_orders shows an approved, signed
  product return registered on 15 June 2026; find_agronomy_invoices shows no credit memo against the
  June herbicide delivery; the return-credit policy's own rule says what a credit memo for returned
  crop protection is and how it is worked out, and it is the only rule in the charter that produces
  one — so the one action that brings the state about is writing that credit memo. Edge 1 runs the
  same way through the overdue invoice and the service-charge policy's own rule.
  At least one problem is the customer's own write: the settlement payment's target tool is
  owner=user, handed over at its place in the order.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
  subject agronomy_credit_memo_issued -> agronomy_returns_and_credits, gate return_inside_window
    (kind time). condition quoted verbatim in solvability_contract. authoritative evidence: the
    billing row for IN-4420915 (invoice_date 2026-06-08, delivery_ticket_number DT-2220671,
    product_category crop_protection). object correlation: correlation_keys
    [[invoice_number, delivery_ticket_number]], bound to the call's invoice_number and
    delivery_ticket_number arguments. time gate: starting business event "the delivery date on the
    ticket it left on", anchor_source agronomy_invoices.invoice_date, clock frozen_time, duration
    variants.return_window_days = 21 for the Seasonal Terms Crop Input Account, counted in whole
    calendar days, relation not_after, boundary inclusive. positive case: delivered 2026-06-08,
    handled 2026-06-18, day 10 of 21 — inside. negative case: delivered 2026-05-27 would be day 22
    — outside, and the correct terminal state would be to write no credit at all. Also inherited and
    satisfied: the programme's returnable classes include crop_protection, and the product is
    unopened, which the approved return request records. The extended policy's overwrite retires
    only the base sentence fixing the credit at the invoiced price less a flat restocking
    percentage; the window, the classes and the unopened requirement stay in force.
  subject agronomy_finance_charge_assessed -> agronomy_finance_charge, gate grace_period_expired
    (kind time). authoritative evidence: IN-4407955 (due_date 2026-03-07, invoice_number, amount).
    correlation_keys [[invoice_number]] bound to the call's invoice_number. time gate: anchor event
    "the due date of that invoice", anchor_source agronomy_invoices.due_date, duration
    variants.finance_charge_grace_days = 15, whole calendar days, due date as day zero, relation
    not_before, boundary exclusive. positive: 103 days have run, far past day 15. negative: had the
    invoice fallen due on 2026-06-04 the handling date would be day 14 and no charge could be
    assessed. The extended policy's two overwrites retire the per-invoice basis and the
    monthly-percentage-on-that-invoice sentence, and nothing else; the grace gate stays in force and
    is the gate above.
  subject agronomy_payment_posted -> agronomy_payment_application, which carries no structured
    eligibility, so the whole policy applies as scope: allowed routes for the Seasonal Terms
    programme are check, ach, credit card and grain settlement transfer; allocation is oldest
    invoice first; the minimum part payment is 25.0 percent of the balance. The member pays by
    electronic bank transfer, an allowed route, and 37030.00 is far above the floor.
    agronomy_credit_standing is additionally cited as input lineage because the extended policy
    reads its reinstatement share, and its sentence on the reinstatement share is declared as
    superseded in overwrite; nothing else of it is touched, and the task writes no reinstatement.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
  Target objects: (1) the crop protection line IN-4420915 / ticket DT-2220671 on account IA-330471 —
  the most recent crop protection delivery, which the return answers; (2) the oldest matured unpaid
  invoice IN-4407955 on the same account, which the month's service charge attaches to; (3) account
  IA-330471 itself, which the payment lands on.
  Correlation keys: invoice_number plus delivery_ticket_number for the credit memo; invoice_number
  for the service charge; account_id for the payment.
  Rows that enter the aggregates: every agronomy_invoices row whose account_id is IA-330471. Rows
  excluded by the same key: the prepay booking BK-770315 and its prepay discount, which sit on the
  Early Pay Prepay Program Account IA-330622 and are therefore outside every SUM and COUNT in all
  three computations, although the member and a careless reader both think of the two accounts as
  one bill.
  Rows already settled: IN-4409120 and IN-4412044 were each cleared in full inside their early pay
  window by PY-903486 and PY-904318, with the discounts 1068.48 and 896.76 granted against them;
  IN-4410953 carries the earlier credit memo of 1016.40 and the part payment PY-912640 of 7999.98.
  The new credit memo is written back against IN-4420915 and no other line, and the new service
  charge against IN-4407955 and no other line.

STEP 1. POLICIES WRITTEN
  agronomy_ext_crop_protection_return_credit (trigger state_due; the cooperative owes the credit
  whether or not the member calls, because the product is already back at the plant against an
  approved signed request). agronomy_ext_arrears_service_charge (state_due; at month-end
  reconciliation the charge should already be on the books). agronomy_ext_arrears_settlement_payment
  (on_request; nobody owes this money until the member asks what to remit and remits it).
  Each policy declares base_policy_refs covering every base policy whose subject intersects its own,
  an explicit overwrite list, cross_category matching its compute exactly, a baseline block whose
  every sentence is verbatim in the rule, and four to six factors.
  FORWARD SWEEP rule -> compute_basis -> compute: every binding that reads the world, aggregates,
  chooses, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence it implements; see the
  compute_basis block of each policy in agronomy.extended.yaml. Sensitive-word cross-check: every
  quotation naming "the ten statement months" or "the twelve statement months" is attached to a
  binding carrying within_months; "apart from those invoiced within the statement months the
  programme's terms cover" is attached to charges_in_terms, which carries
  within_months=P('terms_days') / K('statement_month_days'), 180/30 = 6 on this programme; every "Where ...
  instead" sentence is attached to a ternary; "rounded to two decimal places" is attached to an RND;
  "where that difference is negative the chargeable days are nil" is attached to MX(0, ...); "where
  that total falls under the programme's service charge floor the floor is booked instead" is
  attached to MX(P('finance_charge_minimum_usd'), ...).
  REVERSE SWEEP compute -> rule: every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a binding.
  The combining semantics are pinned in prose and not left to "then": the settlement policy states
  that the reinstatement share and the age step "are combined before they are applied and they do
  not act one after the other"; the return-credit policy states that the restocking charge and the
  handling figure "are each taken off the credited value itself and neither is taken off the other";
  the service-charge policy states the base the rate acts on, the thirty-day statement month, the
  order of relief then collection sum, and that the floor is compared to the total at the end.

STEP 2. TOOLS
  issue_return_credit_6859ca91 (agent, write) — capability card: the desk writes one credit memo
  line on a named crop input account against a named invoice and delivery ticket for a named input
  class; the account's owed balance falls by the credited money; the member sees the credit on the
  next statement; the receipt carries the credit memo's own reference, the invoice, the ticket and
  the money.
  assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa (agent, write) — one service charge line on a named account
  attached to a named overdue invoice; the owed balance rises by the charge; the receipt carries the
  charge line's reference, the invoice and the money.
  post_member_arrears_payment_ad47b93a (user, write) — the member himself posts one payment line
  under his own remittance reference and by a named route; the owed balance falls; the receipt
  carries the payment line's reference, the remittance reference, the route and the money. Owner is
  user because the money is the member's own and only he can move it; it completes on the spot, as
  an electronic transfer he sets up during the call, so nothing waits on an event outside the call.
  None of the three aggregates history, reads a tier table or judges a precondition; each resolves
  the account's customer id for the foreign key, rounds its money argument to the cent and performs
  one ctx.create.
  Gate run after writing them:
    .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_task_tools.py $DIFF
    -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK

STEP 3. THE WORLD, AND WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW IS LOAD-BEARING
  customers: one member; his membership number and mobile are the two credentials the identity
  check needs.
  agronomy_accounts: IA-330471 (Seasonal Terms, past_due since 2026-03-08, credit review 2025-11-14,
  credit standing approved, acres 1180.0, limit 225000.00) carries the programme parameters every
  rate, grace, threshold and charge is read from and the two fields the grace and age ladders rest
  on. Remove the past-due date and the age step falls to nil.
  IA-330622 (Early Pay Prepay) is the excludable trap: it holds 12400.00 of prepay and a 496.00
  credit, and it is what the member has in mind when he says he has money in with the cooperative;
  every aggregate in this task is scoped to the seasonal account, so none of it counts.
  agronomy_invoices, seasonal account: seven invoiced deliveries across two crop years, two early
  pay discounts, three payments, one earlier credit memo, one earlier service charge. Take the two
  discounts off the ladder's reach — by substituting the factor's baseline, which is what an agent
  who never finds its document does — and the charge falls from 320.20 to 314.91, the figure the
  factor_sensitivity run records. Leaving one of them would drop the tier from the whole of them to
  half, and bringing the overdue balance of 103991.04 under the programme's 75000.00 suspension
  threshold would drop it to nil: those are the two things this ladder sorts members by, and both
  are read off the account's own records. Remove the earlier service charge and the overdue clock anchors on the past-due
  date instead, moving the charge to 1155.76. Remove the earlier credit memo and the handling figure
  falls to the split load charge, moving the credit to 15201.00. Remove any of the three payments and
  the monthly rate rises from 0.85 to 1.05 percent. The 2026-04-24 UAN line and the two June lines
  are the in-terms deliveries that must be kept out of the overdue balance; delete them and the
  balance is overstated by 53816.00.
  NEAR-MISSES planted on purpose: (a) the micronutrient line IN-4421140 of 12 June 2026 is the most
  recent delivery on the account, six days back — a reader who takes "the most recent delivery"
  instead of "the most recent crop protection delivery" lands on the prompt return tier of 4.0
  percent and on the wrong quantity and price entirely; the rule excludes it because it is a
  micronutrient line. (b) the earlier herbicide line IN-4410953 is priced at 96.25 against the
  June line's 88.40, which is exactly what the pricing-basis tier selects; a reader who never finds
  that factor uses 88.40. (c) the part payment PY-912640 of 5 February 2026 is four whole months
  back, so it does not fall in the three-month recent window that decides the collection sum,
  although it is within the twelve months that decide the monthly rate. (d) the prepay standing on
  the second account looks like money that should cover the arrears and does not enter any formula.
  agronomy_orders: the approved, signed product return of 15 June 2026. This row is the whole ground
  of the first prerequisite; delete it and there is no reason to write a credit memo at all.
  Cross-product rows, each seeded because a declared factor reads it: custom_service_plans /
  custom_workorders (the live Full-Service Agronomy Plan and its three completed passes decide the
  restocking waiver; delete a pass and the waiver falls from half to a quarter); storage_agreements /
  storage_charges (bushels on hand and the settled storage invoice decide the relief; delete the
  settlement row and the relief falls from a half to three quarters); grain_contracts / grain_ledger
  (15000 bushels still owed at 4.5800 and the January settlement statement decide the grain credit;
  delete the settlement and the share falls from a quarter to a tenth); patronage_memberships /
  patronage_ledger (the January allocation of 9600.00 on 533333.33 input dollars at Class A's declared
  0.0180 a dollar, with its 2880.00 cash portion at that class's 30 percent split and the absence of any cash
  payment decide the patronage offset; add a cash payment row and the share falls from the whole of
  it to a quarter).
  NO OUTCOME STAMPS: nothing in the seed carries a field naming a factor's outcome. The account's
  credit_status and lien_on_file are read as evidence of the credit department's standing decision
  and of the security position, not as a statement about any rate or share. No cache field is used
  as a trap in this task, so no cache/ledger discrepancy is manufactured; the account's
  current_balance of 173003.04 is exactly the sum of the input_receivable deltas on its ledger.
  AUTOMATIC CLAUSES checked row by row before seeding: the past-due flag (already set, and correct
  for an invoice due 2026-03-07); the suspension trigger (45 days or an overdue balance of 75000.00
  on this programme — the account is past due and arguably suspendable, which is precisely why
  buying has been stopped at the plant, but this task books no suspension and none is owed as a
  computed figure); the prepay forfeiture clock on the second account (the booking window closed
  31 December 2025 and the programme forfeits after 24 months, so nothing is forfeit yet); the
  storage paid-through date (2026-04-30, settled); the grain contract's delivery window (opens
  2026-09-01, so no delivery is overdue). None of them ignites an obligation this task set cannot
  carry.

STEP 4. THE PERSONA
  Voice: an unhurried sixty-ish row-crop farmer who says "yep", does not embroider, and treats the
  desk as a neighbour. Organised as a single narrative rather than a form: the situation and the
  request first, then what he will say only when asked, then how he pays, then how he reacts.
  Volunteered at the opening: that the account has stood past due since the early spring; that he wants one
  figure to send in today; that the desk may look at his books and put right what is the
  cooperative's to put right; that he will move the money himself. Every one of those is supported
  by the opening world — the account stands past_due with an invoice unpaid since March.
  Given only when asked: the membership number M-33417, the mobile 5150334471, which of the two
  accounts he means, how the money will come, and the remittance reference PY-448120. He explicitly
  cannot answer what the balance is and refers the desk to the record, which is the must-ask
  question that never enters gold.
  Passive reactions: he accepts whatever the desk tells him is on the account without asking for a
  figure back; he makes the payment himself once it is handed over; he closes once he hears it has
  gone on. The triggers are utterance events ("if he is told ...", "when the agent ... hands the
  payment over", "Once he hears that the payment has gone onto the account"), never DB states, and
  the arc closes exactly where evaluation_criteria closes — his last reaction answers the payment
  and he raises no further work, no document to send and no address to send it to.
  Authority: nothing he says contradicts the record. He does not claim anything has been done, does
  not state a balance, and does not know any computed figure. He never mentions the returned
  chemical or any service charge.

STEP 5. VERIFICATION CODE AND THE GOLD IT PRODUCED

  the gold writes in order with the real share and task tools, and evaluates each policy's compute on
  the snapshot taken immediately before its own step, exactly as check_compute does. It topologically
  sorts the tree first, so the return credit is evaluated on the opening world, the service charge on
  the world after the credit memo has landed, and the settlement payment on the world after both. The
  root problem's figure is deliberately NOT computed on the opening world: on the opening world the
  quoted figure would be 36940.00 and wrong.

STEP 6. EVALUATION AND THE CONVERSATION WALK-THROUGH
  Reads first: locate, verify, then the account record, the whole billing ledger, the agronomy
  requests (which is where the unmet first prerequisite becomes visible), and the field-services plan
  and work orders the restocking waiver rests on. Then the credit memo. Then the storage agreement
  and its charges, and the service charge. Then the grain contracts and ledger and the equity
  membership and ledger, and the member's own payment. Every factor's evidence is pulled by a read
  node before the write that uses it, and the two unmet prerequisites are each discoverable from a
  read node: find_agronomy_orders shows the approved signed return with no credit memo against the
  June delivery, and find_agronomy_invoices shows IN-4407955 unpaid since 7 March with only an April
  service charge on the ledger.
  Turn by turn: he opens with the plant refusing to load and asks for one figure; the desk locates
  him on the membership number and verifies on the mobile; the desk reads the books and tells him a
  credit is owed and a charge is due for the month, to which he answers that the record should be
  followed; the desk works out the figure and hands the payment to him; he makes it and reads back
  the confirmation; the desk tells him it has gone on and he rings off. Every action is carried by a
  synchronous tool under the single frozen_time of 2026-06-18 10:20:00 CDT. Nothing waits on a

Merrill Hollenbeck farms eleven hundred acres of corn and beans out of Bergen with his son, and his family has done business with the cooperative since his father's day. He is unhurried on the telephone, says "yep" more often than he says anything else, and gets to the point without much ceremony. He is ringing in the middle of a wet June because the account has stood past due since the early spring and he has let it run while the weather was against him, and with sidedress still to go he wants it put right today before anyone at the plant has to have that conversation with him. prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, not a fan-out: the settlement payment has one out-edge, to the service charge, and the service charge has one out-edge, to the return credit. There are therefore no parallel prerequisites and no two writes that could be freely reordered. The order is forced twice over by the prerequisite sentences themselves, since the service charge is worked on a balance that the return credit changes and the settlement figure is worked on a ledger that the service charge changes, and the verification run shows both: skipping the return credit moves the charge from 320.20 to 361.10, and skipping the charge moves the quoted figure from 37030.00 to 36940.00.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the service charge write and replaying everything else leaves charges_standing at 745.92 and the settlement base at 103618.08, so the scored payment_amount falls from 37030.00 to 36940.00.

Skipping the return credit write and replaying everything else leaves credits_standing at -1016.40 and the overdue balance at 119187.04, so the scored service_charge_amount rises from 320.20 to 361.10 — and, through it, the scored payment_amount moves as well.
